confidence_note: Book text read. The book gives instructions and reasoning, not a dated scene; no invented episode.
facts: Walking meditation is walking 'not in order to arrive, but just to walk', slowly, alone or with friends, ideally somewhere beautiful, possibly holding a child's hand.
We walk all the time but usually more like running; that prints anxiety and sorrow on the Earth. The aim is to print peace and serenity. Any child can do it.

Outdoors, slightly slower than normal, three steps with each in-breath and three with each out-breath, saying 'In, in, in. Out, out, out.' Naming the breath makes it more real, like saying a friend's name.

If the lungs want four steps give four, if two give two; in and out may differ (three in, four out). Test: 'If you feel happy, peaceful, and joyful while you are walking, you are practicing correctly.'
Notice the contact between feet and Earth; 'Walk as if you are kissing the Earth with your feet.'
On seeing something beautiful (tree, flower, children playing) stop, keep following the breath, then start again.

A Buddhist word means 'wishlessness' or 'aimlessness': nothing placed in front of you to run after because everything is already here. 'We do not try to arrive anywhere.' Thinking of what we want to realize loses our steps.
Washing dishes is both a means and an end; the same holds for walking. 'Every step makes a flower bloom under our feet', if we do not think of past or future.
scene_details: Three steps in, three steps out, 'In, in, in. Out, out, out.'
Feet in contact with the Earth, like kissing it
A child's hand held while walking
Stopping to look at a tree, a flower or children playing, then starting again
tension: A walk whose only rule is that it must not be about arriving anywhere.
opening_idea: The breath count of three steps in, three out, and the permission to take four if the lungs ask for four.

lessons.idea: Treat one ordinary walk as the whole activity instead of the way to the next thing.
lessons.anchor: Walking not in order to arrive, but just to walk; every step as a peaceful step

reflect_final: Which regular walk of your week could you let be only a walk, with no phone and no rehearsing of what comes next?

use_cases.situation: Walking from the car park to a meeting you are nervous about
use_cases.move: Count three steps in and three out for the length of the path and let the meeting wait until the door.
Take their hand and notice how your feet land, instead of checking the time.

use_cases.situation: A break at work that usually goes on the phone
use_cases.move: Walk one lap of the building at a slower pace and stop once to look at something, as the book allows, then start again.

pocket_idea: Make the stretch between two places a walk of its own: three steps in, three out, no arriving.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: The book's walking practice has no destination on purpose.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Hanh's walking meditation: slowly, breath counted in steps, feet felt on the earth, nothing to reach.
conversation_variants.key_contrast_idea: walking to arrive vs walking to walk
